This report analyses a sample of the World Development Indicators (WDI) dataset for 2022. The data source is the World Bank WDI database [@worldbank_wdi].

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

df = pd.read_csv("wdi.csv")
df_clean = df[[
    "gdp_per_capita",
    "life_expectancy",
    "measles_immunisation_rate"
]].dropna()
```
## Exploratory Data Analysis

We focus on three key indicators for 2022: GDP per capita, life expectancy, and inflation rate. These variables capture economic development, health outcomes, and macroeconomic stability.
```{python}
#| label: eda-summary
#| echo: true

df[["gdp_per_capita","life_expectancy","inflation_rate"]].describe()
```
```{python}
#| label: eda-correlation
#| echo: true

df[["gdp_per_capita","life_expectancy","inflation_rate"]].corr()
```
The summary statistics show that GDP per capita is highly dispersed, with large variation across countries. Life expectancy varies within a narrower range, while inflation exhibits strong right-skewness due to several extreme outliers.

The correlation matrix indicates a positive relationship between GDP per capita and life expectancy, suggesting that higher-income countries tend to experience better health outcomes. Inflation appears weakly related to the other two indicators.

## Visualizing Key Relationships

The following plots illustrate the patterns identified in the exploratory analysis.
```{python}
#| label: fig-development-health
#| fig-label: fig-development-health
#| fig-cap: "GDP per capita vs Life Expectancy, colored by measles immunisation rate (2022)."

plt.figure()

scatter = plt.scatter(
    df_clean["gdp_per_capita"],
    df_clean["life_expectancy"],
    c=df_clean["measles_immunisation_rate"]
)

plt.xlabel("GDP per capita")
plt.ylabel("Life expectancy")
plt.title("Economic Development and Health Outcomes")

plt.colorbar(scatter, label="Measles immunisation rate")
plt.show()
```
```{python}
#| label: fig-inflation
#| fig-label: fig-inflation
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of inflation rates across countries (2022)."

plt.figure()

plt.hist(df["inflation_rate"].dropna(), bins=30)

plt.xlabel("Inflation rate")
plt.ylabel("Number of countries")
plt.title("Inflation Rate Distribution (2022)")

plt.show()
```

Figure @fig-development-health visually confirms the positive association between income and life expectancy identified in the correlation analysis. 

Figure @fig-inflation illustrates the right-skewed distribution of inflation, consistent with the presence of extreme outliers observed in the summary statistics.

## Summary of Key Indicators

| Indicator          | Main Observation |
|--------------------|------------------|
| GDP per capita     | Highly dispersed across countries |
| Life expectancy    | Positively associated with GDP |
| Inflation rate     | Right-skewed with extreme outliers |

Table @tbl-key-stats summarises the main statistical patterns identified in the exploratory analysis.

The positive relationship between income and life expectancy is consistent with classic findings in the development literature [@preston1975].
